The Historical and Planned Timeline for the Complete U2C Program Spans More Than 15 Years From Its Conception to Full Operations ................................................................................. 25 viii This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 1 Introduction The transportation industry is entering a new frontier with three simultaneous major transformations: electrification, automation, and on-demand mobility services. All three directly affect the same spaces of transport vehicle technology, roadway infrastructure, and multimodal system operational performance. Further, each area of change adds its own driving forces of complexity to the others’ design challenges. The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) has been studying the related impacts of electrification, automation, and on-demand service on automated/autonomous vehicle (AV) fleets providing public mobility services operating within dense urban environments. Each of these factors in turn affects the emerging future of the multimodal transportation system in the built environment. The initial phases of NLR’s research surveyed early initiatives of AV technology demonstration, with Phase I research documenting 10 early deployment sites in the first edition of The Automated Mobility District Implementation Catalog (Young and Lott 2020).
